title: Exterior Yoneda products surject onto self Ext
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], V an open of Z and n a natural number. Suppose every z∈V has an affine neighborhood of i(z) on which the kernel ideal [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let B=i_*O_Z, G=H^n(RHom_Y(B,B)) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], T=(i*G)|V [def-pc-module-pullback], and E=exteriorSheaf(Hom_Z(i*ker(i),O_Z)|V,n) [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. There exists a morphism φ:E→T whose linear map on every stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] of V is surjective. Injectivity is not asserted.

source.place: Lemma 48.15.4, contraction products and zero-differential Hom calculation; Tag 0BQW, degree-one boundary

proof.text: Apply the Koszul Hom-complex computation to identify the restricted dual of exteriorSheaf(i*ker(i),n) with the desired self Ext pullback T. This computation does not involve the exterior power of the dual.

Construct the existing determinant-evaluation morphism exteriorSheaf(C dual,n)→dual(exteriorSheaf C n). Each supplied regular chart gives a conormal basis, hence a finite free conormal frame; the determinant pairing is bijective on sections of every subopen of that chart. Represent a target germ on such a subopen and lift it through the section map to prove stalk surjectivity. Obtain the upstream exteriorPower pairing p₀ and its determinant formula. Define p as exteriorSheafPowerIso(dual C,n).hom followed by p₀ and then dualFunctor.mapIso(exteriorSheafPowerIso(C,n).op).hom. Apply the upstream local pairing theorem directly to p₀. Both comparison section maps are bijections; Function.Bijective.comp gives bijectivity of p on every subopen. This replaces conjugation and cancellation with forward composition, retaining the same stalk-surjectivity argument.

Open restriction of exterior powers gives E≅(exteriorSheaf(C dual,n))|V. Naturality of the restriction-stalk isomorphism transfers surjectivity of the determinant morphism to V. Compose the inverse exterior-restriction isomorphism, that restricted determinant morphism, and the Koszul comparison isomorphism. On stalks the two isomorphisms are surjective; lifting an element successively through the three maps proves the composite is surjective. For the upstream restriction theorem, rewrite exteriorPower as exteriorSheaf at the module and its restriction using [lem-sc-exterior-sheaf-upstream-comparison]; this preserves exactly the legacy objects used by the rest of the argument.

lean.statement:
theorem koszulRegularImmersion_self_ext_yoneda_surjection
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (V : Z.Opens) (n : ℕ)
    (hregular : ∀ z : Z, z ∈ V → ∃ U : Y.affineOpens, i z ∈ U.1 ∧
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
        Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    let T := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G)
    let E := Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
        (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := Z.sheaf)
          ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules)
          (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf))) n
    ∃ φ : E ⟶ T, ∀ z : V.toScheme, Function.Surjective (φ.stalkLinearMap z)
